note: MAPPING: code derivation pattern 1 -- data/degirolamo_2022_covid_wellbeing.py keeps the source CSV column names pag14_1_1..5 as item codes (no rename, no positional step, no reverse-coding; resp stored as deposited 1-7). Io penso che ...)'; 5/5 labels and all 7 value labels are byte-identical across the four wave dictionaries. ENGLISH (translation_source=mixed): item_text_translated is the deposit's own WHO/COSMO English template codebook, rows Pag_14_1_1..5 (codes tie 1:1 to pag14_1_1..5), trailing spaces stripped; that file truncates item 5 at 'There are secret organizations that greatly influence political ' and the final word 'decisions' was restored from Bruder et al. source_ref: OSF osf.io/3527a (MECO L1, licence CC-By Attribution 4.0 International per the node's licence record), release 2.0/version 2.1: wave 1/auxiliary files/reading task materials/comp-questions.xlsx (osf.io/download/h7b2z, sha256 1cc62660bf7fdeddc47631da174dee8146780233e7edadbf3cc7cb947051dab1; 13 sheets du..tr, columns number,q1,a1..q4,a4; byte-identical to release 1.2 uch24); wave 1 supp texts.xlsx (mz48p, sha256 afba00c45cfd90814ae992ac00e920c1454d62ae579867370fb4be0adfebf8cc); wave 2 supp texts_wave2.xlsx (nukg9, sha256 ae1e2b8045a46ac633097995e3c7fab120c82f2ab6e570aacfce57987b499102, Sheet1 texts, Sheet2 'dif' notes); all-back-translations.xlsx (wave 1 c3fv5/pm5vk, sha256 b385ec7266897362e805c956612861bca6a41c40fffebde99838a9ac681dbcde) and all-back-translations-W2.xlsx (5ajeb, sha256 468aac9f6840d9deb46f04c326d661b152f96eaea14229f24292c2fc5aca475c); wave 2 auxiliary bitmaps.zip (3eu49; text-passage images only, no question screens); readmes g5ysd (wave 1) and 8c4bd/8veag (wave 2). Papers: Siegelman et al. 2022 BRM 10.3758/s13428-021-01772-6; wave 2 Scientific Data 10.1038/s41597-025-05453-3 (Methods: 'Each of the 12 texts was followed by four yes/no comprehension questions'; answered with the 1 ('yes') and 0 ('no') keys). IRW script data/meco_l1_comprehension.py (item-code derivation reproduced offline: 708/708 codes).
note: ITEM CODES: data/meco_l1_comprehension.py builds item from the release's (site, text number trialid/number, QUESTIONNUM): text{t}_q{q} for the 20 questions on the five matched texts (1,3,7,11,12) shared by every site, {site}_text{t}_q{q} for deviant/site-specific matched cells, {version}_text{t}_q{q} for local texts. I re-ran that derivation offline from the cached OSF files (no network call through the script, whose User-Agent carries an email) and it reproduces all 708 live codes exactly. comp-questions.xlsx is keyed by the same text number (column number) and question column q1..q4, so wording and key attach by that label (mapping_basis=paper_explicit). COVERAGE: 391 of 708 items carry question wording and correct_response: 20 shared matched-text items take the English sheet's wording (base field English), 371 site/version-specific items take their wave-1 site's sheet in the administered language, with English in item_text_translated. 317 items ship item_text and correct_response BLANK, because wave 2 published no question wording anywhere in the deposit (no comp-questions file in wave 2/auxiliary files; the accuracy .rda holds only uniform_id/lang/number/QUESTIONNUM/ACCURACY; bitmaps.zip holds passage images only): ru_mo 48, ba 32, bp 28, ch_s 28, ch_t 28, da 28, ic 28, se 28, ge_v2 24, hi 24, sp_ch 12, hi_iiith 4, hi_iitk 4, plus no_text6_q4 (below). These rows still carry the passage. SECTIONS: section_id = one passage version (text{t} for the shared matched items, else {version}_text{t}); section_prompt = that version's passage from supp texts.xlsx / supp texts_wave2.xlsx in the administered language (shared text{t} sections carry the English passage). section_prompt_translated = the study's own English back-translation from all-back-translations(-W2).xlsx (wave-2 'ch' row used for both ch_s and ch_t, 'ge' for ge_v2, 'hi' for hi and hi_iiith). hi_iitk_text5_q1..q4 ship section_prompt blank: supp texts_wave2.xlsx Sheet2 marks IITK text 5 'dif', but the Sheet1 'Hindi iitk' row is character-identical to 'Hindi iiith' for all 12 texts, so IITK's own text 5 is not in any text source (only in bitmaps.zip as an image). TRANSLATION: item_text_translated for the 343 non-English questions was machine-translated by this project (the deposit's back-translations cover passages only); section_prompt_translated is study_supplied. Hence translation_source=mixed. option_text 'Correct'/'Incorrect' are IRW scoring labels for resp (resp is ACCURACY, 1 correct / 0 incorrect, as the release scores it), following the trivia_fastrich_2017/twod_rotation_mather2023 precedent; they are not administered text. correct_response = 'yes'/'no' transcribed from the sheet's a1..a4 (1 = yes, 0 = no per the papers' key description) -- key source_published. instructions left blank: the papers describe the procedure but print no literal participant-facing instruction. DEVIATIONS FROM LITERAL: (a) the Spanish sheet is mojibake throughout (UTF-8 read as cp1255, e.g. 'ֲ¿' for '¿', 'mֳ¡s' for 'más'); repaired by the exact byte round-trip (encode cp1255 -> decode UTF-8), which succeeds on every Spanish cell shipped; (b) a stray trailing ' "' removed from gr_text5_q1; (c) leading/trailing whitespace trimmed; (d) passages: literal '\n' markers (English, Basque, Chinese simplified, Icelandic, Norwegian W2) converted to line breaks, and the '*' word-segmentation markers in the Chinese (simplified) row removed -- checked against bitmaps.zip Chinese_Simplified_2.png, which shows no asterisks. SITE ASSUMPTIONS INHERITED FROM THE PROCESSING SCRIPT: wave-2 sites that reused a wave-1 text verbatim (no, tr, en_uk with en, ge_po/ge_zu text 8) share that wave-1 version's item codes, so they get the wave-1 wording; nothing published confirms they reused the questions as well. Shared text{t}_q{q} items are answered in 18-20 languages (language lists them per item); only the English wording ships. QUIRKS IN THE SOURCE: Norwegian sheet text 6 q4 repeats q3's wording with the opposite key (0 vs 1); the wave-1 readme says 'Due to a human error, in the Norwegian sample there are 47 comprehension questions', and the live data hold 0 wave-1 Norwegian responses to no_text6_q4 (42 to each of q1-q3); its 19 responses are wave-2 Norwegian, whose wording is unpublished, so no_text6_q4 ships blank. Spanish sheet text 3 q3 repeats q4's wording (both key no); shipped literally as sp_text3_q3, and the data agree: Spanish accuracy 0.479 on it vs 0.521 on text3_q4, against 0.930 for text3_q3 at the other wave-1 sites. POSSIBLE SCORING DEFECTS IN THE RESPONSE DATA (not changed here; correct_response ships the sheet key, which is the key the stored accuracy reflects): he_text1_q3 asks whether Janus's temple doors were CLOSED in peacetime -- true per the Hebrew passage and its back-translation ('closed in times of peace') -- but carries the English item's key 'no'; only 0.298 of 47 Hebrew readers are scored correct, against 0.70-1.00 on the other text-1 items, i.e. ~70% answered 'yes' and were scored wrong. ru_text12_q4 (a statement that regional authorities in some countries may introduce their own plates; the Russian back-translation says registers are kept 'in separate states or regions' in some countries) also carries key 'no' and scores 0.370 (46 readers) against 0.80-0.96 on Russian text12_q1-q3 -- the same pattern, less clear-cut. RIGHTS: the questions and passages are the study's own reading materials, published in the CC BY 4.0 OSF deposit; not a third-party instrument, so the instrument rights register does not apply; no restriction located.
public_note: Item text is published for wave-1 sites only: 317 of 708 items (all wave-2-only versions: Basque, Brazilian Portuguese, Chinese, Danish, Icelandic, Serbian, Hindi, Chilean Spanish, German wave 2 and Russian wave 2) carry the reading passage but no question wording, because wave 2 never released its questions; the 20 shared matched-text items show the English wording although they were answered in 18-20 languages (language lists them per item); English item_text_translated is a machine translation by IRW; and he_text1_q3 (and probably ru_text12_q4) appear to be scored against the wrong key in the response data -- the Hebrew question was reworded to 'closed' while keeping the English 'no' key, and 70% of readers are scored incorrect.
